bottom_line: This is a correlated, factor-style de-risking of semiconductors, not a verdict on the AI hardware fundamentals that the headlines still describe as supply-constrained. SOXX is down 27.3% in a month and 37.4% from its 52-week high, only 1 of 33 tracked stocks rose last week, and the segments are moving together (equipment/test correlation 0.92, AI compute/interconnect 0.89). The market is trading the second derivative (peak growth, crowded positioning, rising volatility) against first-derivative evidence that memory, EUV and advanced packaging remain sold out. The credit tape says the stress is real but narrow: CCC OAS is up 303bp in three months while BBB and BB, the issuers that fund fabs and AI capex, have widened only 19bp and 52bp. The view changes if HY ex-CCC (B/BB) spreads start to follow CCC wider, or if the next round of memory and equipment guidance stops being raised.

themes.title: Price and fundamentals have decoupled: the selloff is a positioning and second-derivative event, not a demand miss
themes.thesis: The reported fundamentals in memory and the semiconductor equipment chain are still described as supply-constrained: SK hynix is reported to say DRAM and HBM are sold out through 2029, memory makers are reported to earn roughly 80% margins, and ASM, Tokyo Electron and Intel's CTO all point to tight capacity. Yet memory is 48.6% below its high and equipment 48.1% below. When the best news in a cycle stops lifting prices (SanDisk's beat-and-raise sold off) the market is usually discounting the rate of change, not the level: peak margins and peak growth can be bullish for earnings and bearish for multiples at the same time. A market that is already priced for long scarcity has little room for upside surprises, so any sign of order timing, customer double-ordering or AI-capex digestion is magnified. This is consistent with a regime where valuation resets until estimates re-accelerate, but the packet does not contain order, inventory or capex-guide data to confirm or rule out a genuine demand pause.
falsifiers: A major memory or equipment company cuts quarterly revenue or capex guidance, or reports order cancellations/push-outs.
Spot or contract DRAM/HBM pricing rolls over in a reputable price series (TrendForce, DRAMeXchange), unlike the single-source spike reports.
Prices keep falling after clear upward estimate revisions through the next earnings cycle, which would indicate a structural de-rating rather than temporary positioning.

themes.title: Correlation spike with a defensive pocket: semis are trading as one factor, with mobile/RF diverging
themes.thesis: Cross-sectional dispersion is narrow relative to the size of the move: over one month the median stock is -25.2% with a standard deviation of 15.3pp and only 6% of names positive. The segment correlation matrix shows the AI-linked cluster moving almost as one trade (equipment/test-packaging 0.92, AI compute/interconnect 0.89, AI compute/foundry 0.88 over 60 days). The notable break is mobile/RF, whose correlation with the other segments has fallen by 0.22 to 0.30 versus the prior 60-day window and is the only segment with positive three-month performance (+14.7%). That pattern is what a crowded-factor unwind looks like: the stocks sharing the 'AI capex' exposure fall together irrespective of their own fundamentals, while less crowded franchises are spared. For stock selection this means the information content of individual price moves is currently low, and the bounce, when it comes, is likely to be just as correlated.
falsifiers: 60-day correlations between AI-linked segments fall back toward 0.6-0.7 while returns stay negative, which would indicate selling has become idiosyncratic.
Mobile/RF's relative strength reverses and it sells off sharply with the group, which would suggest it was only lagging, not defensive.

themes.title: Credit stress is real but confined to the weakest tier; the funding channel for AI capex is not yet impaired
themes.thesis: HY OAS is at 348bp, up 77bp in three months and in the 100th percentile of its one-year range, and IG OAS at 93bp is also at a one-year extreme. But the widening is concentrated in the weakest rating bucket: CCC OAS is 13.2% (+303bp over 3M, +435bp over 1Y), B is 3.67% (+80bp 3M), while BB is 2.13% (+52bp) and BBB is 1.16% (+19bp). The large semis and hyperscalers are generally investment-grade or BB-area issuers (background knowledge, not in the packet), so the cost of capital for the main AI-capex builders has risen modestly rather than closed. The spread-implied annual loss proxy of 5.8% (OAS 3.48% / (1 - 40% recovery)) is a stress gauge only, but it is consistent with the VIX at 28. Realised bank credit quality is benign but stale: business-loan delinquency was 1.27% (25th percentile) and charge-offs 0.58% as of April 2026, so there is no evidence yet in the packet that defaults have turned. The semis link is risk-appetite: SOXX daily returns correlate -0.55 with HY OAS changes over 60 days (-0.45 over 120).
falsifiers: BB OAS rises above roughly 300bp or BBB above 150bp, i.e. the widening migrates up the ratings ladder to the capex funders.
CCC OAS retraces most of its 3M move while semis keep falling, which would break the credit/semis link.
A published rated-bond default rate (Moody's/S&P) rising sharply would convert the spread signal from a risk-premium to a credit-loss story.

themes.title: Policy remains an optional upside, not a base case, for Nvidia's China exposure
themes.thesis: Week-long policy flow is a cluster of conflicting and partly unverified reports. The US is reported to have approved some chip sales to China-linked firms (He94c0a1), but Chosunbiz reports that China is stalling H200 imports to favour domestic AI chips (Hedb8c35) and another outlet says China is no longer rushing to buy (Hdd610d3). In the month window, Reuters reported new Chinese export curbs around AI-related technology (H023d22d) and Nvidia's CEO argued that US curbs accelerated China's chip push (H645ab63). Taken together, the strongest inference is that revenue from China is being limited from both sides, so it should be modelled as option value with timing risk, not baseline demand. Allegations about espionage involving Nvidia's chief executive (Hee75e87, H512b429) come from low-reliability sources and should be treated as unverified political noise.
falsifiers: Nvidia discloses material H200 China shipments in a filing or earnings call.
A primary-source US licence notice or Chinese customs/regulator statement confirms or ends the import stall.
